gloss: hypocenter; epicenter; source of a quake

definitions.explanation: The point of origin of an earthquake, either underground (hypocenter) or its projection on the surface (epicenter). A key term in earthquake-related news and information.
Figuratively, the origin or source of trouble, conflict, or a problem.

examples.japanese: {震源|しんげん}は{海底|かいてい}だった。
examples.english: The hypocenter was under the sea.

examples.japanese: {震源|しんげん}の{深|ふか}さは{約|やく}10キロだった。
examples.english: The depth of the hypocenter was about 10 kilometers.

examples.japanese: {気象庁|きしょうちょう}は{震源|しんげん}が{内陸|ないりく}の{浅|あさ}い{場所|ばしょ}であると{発表|はっぴょう}した。
examples.english: The Meteorological Agency announced that the hypocenter was at a shallow inland location.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}が{問題|もんだい}の{震源|しんげん}だ。
examples.english: He is the source of the problem.

examples.japanese: その{部署|ぶしょ}が{社内|しゃない}トラブルの{震源|しんげん}になっている。
examples.english: That department is the source of internal trouble.

examples.japanese: {経済危機|けいざいきき}の{震源|しんげん}がどこにあるのか、{専門家|せんもんか}の{間|あいだ}でも{意見|いけん}が{分|わ}かれている。
examples.english: Even among experts, opinions are divided on where the source of the economic crisis lies.

notes:
USAGE:
{震源|しんげん} combines {震|しん} (quake, tremor) and {源|げん} (source, origin). Strictly speaking, {震源|しんげん} refers to the underground point (hypocenter), while {震源地|しんげんち} refers to the surface location (epicenter), though the terms are often used interchangeably in casual speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {震源|しんげん}の{深|ふか}さ (depth of the hypocenter)
- {震源地|しんげんち} (epicenter location)
- {震源|しんげん}に{近|ちか}い (close to the epicenter)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{震源地|しんげんち} specifically refers to the surface point above the earthquake origin. {震源|しんげん} is more general and is also the form used in figurative senses.
